alternates.speaker: Tulsidas
alternates.setting: Tulsidas on what is left when every other practice feels out of reach.
alternates.sanskrit: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलंबन एकू॥ कालनेमि कलि कपट निधानू। नाम सुमति समरथ हनुमानू ॥
alternates.line: When no practice, devotion or wisdom seems within reach, the name of Ram is still a support.
alternates.translation: In this age there is no ritual action, no devotion and no discernment left to lean on; the name of Ram is the one support. In the age of Kali, the name is the clever Hanuman against Kalanemi, the master of deceit.

verse.line: No winter was but summer came behind,
verse.translation: No winter was but summer came behind, Each hollow crests the wave, They push each other in light and shade; Be steady then and brave.
verse.why: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

prasang.title: 'Hold on yet a while, brave heart' (poem to the Maharaja of Khetri)
prasang.summary: A short poem of encouragement to a friend. Clouds hide the sun for a while, summer always follows winter, and no honest struggle is wasted even when hopes fail.
prasang.lesson: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verse.sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥
verse.line: There is a joy you grow into through practice, one that brings sorrow to an end.
verse.translation: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, best of the Bharatas: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, and in which one reaches the end of sorrow.
verse.why: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

prasang.title: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

why: there is a joy that is grown into, not found ready-made
practice is how it is reached

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verse.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचपार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥
verse.line: Whoever does good never comes to ruin, my friend. Not here, not after.
verse.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Partha, there is no ruin for him either in this world or the next. No one who does good, my friend, ever comes to grief.
verse.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

why: frees a person to try again
No one who does good is lost and no effort is wasted: the ground under someone who thinks it was all for nothing.

verse.speaker: Sampati
verse.setting: Sampati, his wings regrown, urges the monkeys who had given up the search.
verse.sanskrit: जो नाघइ सत जोजन सागर। करइ सो राम काज मति आगर॥ मोहि बिलोकि धरहु मन धीरा। राम कृपाँ कस भयउ सरीरा ॥
verse.line: Look at me and take heart. My burned wings have grown back.
verse.translation: Whoever can leap the hundred-league ocean, wise and capable, will do Ram's work. Look at me and take heart: see what Ram's grace has done to my body.
verse.why: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.

prasang.title: Sampati's burned wings
prasang.summary: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's messengers. He tells them where Sita is, and his wings grow back as he speaks.
prasang.story_hook: The monkeys had given up and were waiting to die when a vulture with no wings spoke to them.
prasang.lesson: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.

why: a party that had sat down to die gets up
grace has visibly acted once already

story.title: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf
story.story_hook: The whole world was one dark ocean, and on it floated a single banyan tree with a child asleep on a branch.
story.summary: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
story.lesson: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
story.hook_title: An old sage drifted alone over a drowned world, and found a child asleep on a leaf
story.teaser: An old sage drifted alone over a drowned world, and found a child asleep on a leaf
